questions.question: Derive the expression for the magnetic field at a point on the axis of a current-carrying circular coil using Biot–Savart law.
questions.solution:
For a coil of radius a carrying current I, each element dl is perpendicular to the position vector from the element to an axial point distance x away, and perpendicular components cancel by symmetry.

dB = (μ₀I dl)/(4π(a²+x²)); the axial component is dB·cosθ with cosθ = a/√(a²+x²).

Integrating over 2πa: **B = μ₀Ia²/(2(a²+x²)^{3/2})**. At the centre (x = 0): B = μ₀I/2a.
questions.knowledgeNote: Perpendicular components cancel because opposite elements contribute equal and opposite sideways fields — always state this symmetry argument for full marks.

questions.question: What is a cyclotron? Derive the expression for the cyclotron frequency and explain why it cannot accelerate electrons to very high energies.
questions.solution:
A cyclotron accelerates charged particles in a magnetic field between two dees with an alternating potential.

The magnetic force supplies the centripetal force: qvB = mv²/r → r = mv/qB. Period T = 2πr/v = 2πm/qB, so **f = qB/2πm**, independent of speed.

As the particle speeds up, relativistic mass increases, so the revolution frequency falls out of step with the oscillator and resonance is lost — hence the energy limit.
questions.knowledgeNote: The cyclotron frequency is mass-dependent, so the constant-frequency design only works while m ≈ m₀.

questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω gives a full-scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. How will you convert it into (a) an ammeter of range 1 A and (b) a voltmeter of range 10 V?
questions.solution:
**(a) Ammeter:** shunt S in parallel — S = I_gG/(I − I_g) = (10⁻³ × 100)/(1 − 10⁻³) = **0.1 Ω** (approximately), i.e. a very small shunt.

**(b) Voltmeter:** series resistance R = V/I_g − G = 10/10⁻³ − 100 = 10 000 − 100 = **9900 Ω**.
questions.knowledgeNote: An ideal ammeter has zero resistance (shunt in parallel); an ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance (high series resistance).
